events.did: 坐在代代相传的樱桃木桌前；桌面近乎全黑、布满疤痕与污渍，讲述祖先历史；女人们在这桌上切草药、编织家族、研制治疗与防护的咒语、泼洒酒液仰头大笑、守着冒泡的坩埨（肥皂或炖菜、药酒或酊剂、掺了魔法与奇迹的药剂）；布莱尔女巫像一串琥珀珠子般延绵到 1600 年代，聚在此处分担过去的重负、谋划未来、品味当下，靠姐妹情谊的圆环彼此守护
events.verbatim: Helena sat at the cherry wood table passed down to the Blair women through generations. The patina was nearly black, pitted with scars and stains eloquently describing the history of their ancestors. Women cut herbs at this table, knitted together the fabric of their family, devised spells for healing and protection, spilled wine as they threw back their heads and laughed while watching a cauldron bubble with soap or stew, tonics or tinctures, potions ripe with magic and miracles. Blair women strung together like beads of amber, stretching back to the 1600s, all gathered here to share burdens from the past, devise plans for the future, and savour the sweetness of the present, safe in the circle of sisterhood that bound them.

events.did: 把一杯冒热气的蒲公英茶放到海伦娜面前，说「喝」
events.verbatim: Aunt Rowan placed a steaming cup of dandelion tea in front of Helena. ‘Drink.’

events.did: 蒲公英茶有净化之效，也许能冲开阻塞海伦娜天赋的东西；姨妈用蜂蜜和自己的治愈之力调甜；海伦娜吹凉后啜饮
events.verbatim: Dandelion tea had cleansing properties. It might flush out whatever blocked Helena’s gift. Aunt Rowan had sweetened the mixture with honey and a dash of her own healing powers. Helena blew on the surface until it cooled, then sipped.

events.did: 说「这从未发生过」；藏不住担忧；哈姆雷特用头顶她的小腿，她把手伸到桌下抚在它两耳之间
events.verbatim: ‘This has never happened before.’ She couldn’t hide her worry as Hamlet bumped his head against her leg. She reached under the table to rest her hand between his ears.

events.did: 冲进厨房，雪白的雪貂奥菲利娅像活披肩一样缠在她肩上
events.verbatim: ‘What is wrong?’ Ellie swept into the kitchen, her snow-white ferret, Ophelia, wrapped around her shoulders like a living stole.

events.did: 说「有东西挡住了你表姐的天赋」；叙述者点出她从不在问题外围绕圈子，能一刀从正中劈开
events.verbatim: ‘Something is blocking your cousin’s powers.’ Aunt Rowan never spoke around a problem when she could just as easily rip right through the centre.

events.did: 金发蓝眼，说「Hel，那太糟了」；坐到长凳上把手放在海伦娜手臂上；奥菲利娅眨着粉眼从肩头跑去找哈姆雷特（一见钟情）；雪貂与狐狸不可能在一起，但这对彼此倾心的魔宠们意义不大；「你的气场有点……不对劲」
events.verbatim: Ellie’s blonde brows, only a few shades darker than her bright hair, creased over bluebell eyes. ‘Hel, that’s awful.’ She plunked herself on the bench next to Helena and put her soft hand on Helena’s arm. Ophelia perked up, blinking her pink eyes as she scurried off Ellie’s shoulder to find her one true love, Hamlet. That a ferret and a fox could never be together meant little to the familiars who doted on each other. ‘Your aura is a little…’ she scrunched her nose, ‘off.’

events.did: 埃莉先说「有点 shimmery」，改口「murky」，再改成「foggy」；海伦娜脊背僵硬反问「你说 off 是什么意思」；随后自嘲「我的力量在失灵、我的气场雾蒙蒙的，这真是好兆头」
events.verbatim: Helena stiffened her spine. ‘What do you mean, off?’ Ellie shrugged. ‘Just shimmery. No, that’s not right. Murky… or what’s another word for muddy, but not so unpleasant? Foggy! Your aura is a little foggy.’ Helena was used to Ellie’s meandering conversations, but a foggy aura was incredibly unhelpful at this juncture. ‘Wonderful. My powers are failing, and my aura is foggy. This certainly bodes well.’

events.did: 说从未听说气场雾蒙蒙能杀人（但不确定）；「最坏情况是摔一跤，不过有时候摔一跤反而是好事」；她一直想飞
events.verbatim: Ellie flapped her hand, as if she could shoo away Helena’s dire mood as easily as a bad odour. ‘Oh, don’t be such a grump. A foggy aura never killed anyone. At least, I don’t think it ever has. Have you ever heard of a witch dying from a foggy aura, Aunt Rowan?’ But she didn’t pause to hear an answer. ‘At the worst, you might trip in the fog and fall, but sometimes, falling is the best thing, don’t you think? I mean, how are flying and falling really that different? And I’ve always wanted to fly.’

events.did: 嘀咕「区别在于最后那声巨响」；并试图不去想象自己带着雾蒙蒙气场、力量被封，摔得四分五裂的样子
events.verbatim: ‘I imagine it’s the resounding crash at the end that separates the two,’ muttered Helena, trying not to imagine herself splattered on the ground with her foggy aura and blocked powers.

events.did: 辩解「我不是 grump，只是我看见雨云而你们只看见彩虹，这让我不是怪人而是现实主义者」；随即自己也觉得语气像在发脾气
events.verbatim: ‘I’m not a grump, you know. Just because I see rain clouds when all you notice is the rainbow doesn’t make me a grouch. It makes me a realist.’ Helena cringed. Because she sounded like a grump.

events.did: 评价「作为被赋予魔法的女人，现实主义恐怕不是明智的立场」
events.verbatim: ‘As a woman endowed with magic, realism hardly seems a wise perspective, does it?’ Aunt Rowan’s dry observation didn’t help.

events.did: 爬上桌腿再一次绕上埃莉肩膀，对海伦娜吱吱叫，替女主人抱不平
events.verbatim: Ophelia scurried up the leg of the table to wind once more around Ellie’s shoulders. She chittered at Helena, taking offence on behalf of her mistress.

events.did: 海伦娜深呼吸再试，承认「也许我是有那么一点 grump」；埃莉问是否所有能力都受影响；海伦娜说「不，我还能操控我的元素」，并召出一股水花扫过房间、给所有植物洒上露水作为证明
events.verbatim: Helena took a deep breath and tried again. ‘All right. Maybe I am a little bit of a grump. But you would be too if your magic was malfunctioning.’ Ellie tapped her finger thoughtfully against her chin. ‘Are all of your abilities affected?’ ‘No. I can still control my element.’ To prove her point, a swirl of water appeared between them. With a flick of her eyes, it swept through the room, distributing dew on all the plants.

events.did: 咂嘴说「你总是浇得太多」；挥手让露水消失；厨房里每片叶子、蕨叶与花瓣一起愉悦地颤抖
events.verbatim: Aunt Rowan tsked. ‘You always overwater them.’ She waved her hand and the dew disappeared. Every leaf, frond, and petal in the kitchen collectively shivered with pleasure.

events.did: 说「我只是证明我的力量还在。我能读人心。只是读不了她的」——把 “her” 当诅咒般说出来；因为辛西娅正变成一个她摆脱不掉的 hex（咒），一场压倒性的瘟疫侵入她的感官：只闻得到忍冬与香草、只看得见辛西娅 pixie 形眼睛里绿与棕的条纹、只听得到辛西娅的低语；这让人发疯、让人分心、让人陶醉；难怪她无法专注于自己的手艺
events.verbatim: ‘I’m just proving my powers still work. I can read people’s thoughts. Just not hers.’ Helena said the last word like a curse. Because Cynthia was becoming a hex Helena couldn’t shake. An overwhelming plague infiltrating her senses until all she could smell was honeysuckle and vanilla. All she could see were the striations of green and brown in Cynthia’s pixie-shaped eyes. All she could hear was the low melody of Cynthia’s voice. It was maddening. And distracting. And intoxicating. No wonder she couldn’t concentrate on her craft.

events.did: 挑眉问「她？说的是哪个她？肯定不是我那位新嫂子。你从一开始就不喜欢那个她」
events.verbatim: Ellie raised a brow. ‘Her? Exactly which her are we talking about? Certainly not my new sister-in-law. You haven’t liked that particular her from the start.’

events.did: 海伦娜说「我还没那么在乎那个女人到要去讨厌她的地步」；埃莉优雅地哼了一声表示不赞同——叙述者点破这是说谎
events.verbatim: ‘I don’t care enough about the woman to dislike her.’ Ellie’s delicate snort begged to differ. Liar.

events.did: 说对那个搅乱她能力的可恶女人很有意见，尤其是辛西娅最近在自家血泊中发现了丈夫，而她的技能本可帮忙判定谁杀了他；偏偏她读不到辛西娅的念头，而这些念头可能让辛西娅卷进他的死
events.verbatim: Helena ignored her and continued. ‘But I do take exception to the vexatious woman blocking my powers. Especially as she most recently found her husband in a pool of his own blood and my skills would be very helpful in determining who killed him. Rather convenient that I can’t read her thoughts when they could implicate Cynthia in his death.’

events.did: 摇头说「我本该窥探可怜人的未来，也许能让他免于这种惨烈结局。不过若传言属实，也许不能。命运有平衡天平的本事，我不认为侯爵在讨好它们的 favor」；她对伯罗斯勋爵之死知情，因为布莱尔女巫之间没有秘密；但她的能力对调查无用
events.verbatim: Ellie shook her head, her lips turning down in a sad frown. ‘I should have peeked into the poor man’s future. Mayhap I could have saved him from such a terrible end. Although, if the gossip is true, perhaps not. The fates have a way of balancing the scales, and I don’t think the marquess was courting their favour.’ Ellie huffed out a contemplative breath. She was well aware of Lord Burrows’ murder, as there were no secrets amongst the Blair women, but her particular powers would be of no help in the investigation.

events.did: 埃莉的能力属风系，助她做出令人不安的精准未来幻象，也让她能读气场；但伯罗斯已死，窥探他的未来无用，也看不见死人的气场
events.verbatim: Ellie was tied to the air, and that ephemeral element aided in her disconcertingly accurate visions of the future. It also lent her skill in reading auras. But Lord Hubert Burrows’ death had already occurred, so peering into his future was useless. And she could hardly see a dead man’s aura.

events.did: 主动替海伦娜值第二天的班，好让表姐能陪拉奇兰叔叔去讯问伯罗斯夫人；叙述者评「非常体贴」，而海伦娜表现得像忘恩负义的人
events.verbatim: Instead, she had volunteered to cover Helena’s shift on the morrow so her cousin could accompany Uncle Lachlan to interview Lady Burrows. Which was incredibly kind. And Helena was acting like an ungrateful wretch.

events.did: 承诺回程去 Barty’s Confectionery 买煮柠檬糖给埃莉当谢礼；表姐对甜食上瘾、尤其喜欢柠檬糖；Barty 就在他们 Savile Row 店铺三门之外
events.verbatim: She promised herself she would visit Barty’s Confectionery on her return from Cynthia’s interview and buy Ellie some boiled lemon drops as a thank you for all her help. Her cousin was addicted to anything sweet but had a particular weakness for the lemon drops Barty sold. As he was conveniently located three doors down from their shop on Savile Row, it would be no trouble.

events.did: 罗恩姨妈在她们逃离苏格兰后开设 All Things Bright and Beautiful，在伦敦闹市找到更广阔的社会；她的药剂铺如今是全城顶级美容店；上流社会女士花大价钱买 Clio 与罗恩姨妈制作的高端产品，为布莱尔女巫们提供奢华生活；主要对手 Madame Rachel 偏爱把砷、铅与白垩掺进有毒混合物；All Things Bright and Beautiful 依靠在效力巅峰采收的天然成分、极度用心准备，若有一点魔法助效则「那是另一回事」
events.verbatim: Aunt Rowan opened All Things Bright and Beautiful when they fled Scotland and found a broader society in the bustling centre of London. Her apothecary was now the city’s premier beauty shop. Ladies of the beau monde paid exorbitant fees for the high-end products Clio and Aunt Rowan created, providing the Blair women with a lavish lifestyle they all enjoyed. Unlike their main competitor, Madame Rachel, who preferred to blend arsenic, lead, and chalk into her toxic mixtures, All Things Bright and Beautiful relied on natural ingredients harvested at peak potency and prepared with the utmost care. If a dash of magic aided in their effectiveness, that was neither here nor there.

events.did: 说「辛西娅连蜘蛛都舍不得踩死」；叙述者点出她忠诚到极点，不容忍任何人对她爱的人说不善——而这几乎包括她遇见的每个人
events.verbatim: ‘Cynthia wouldn’t squash a spider,’ Ellie continued. She was loyal to a fault and wouldn’t tolerate anyone speaking unkindly about those she loved. With Ellie, that included almost everyone she met.

events.did: 说「我听说过。但即便好人也能干下黑事」；母亲的脸像远方的梦一样闪了一下，她眨眼驱散回忆专注当下；无论辛西娅是否有罪，她肯定要为阻断自己的力量负责；若能听见她的念头，也许能洗清她的嫌疑；难道自己是在帮她也这么难相信？
events.verbatim: ‘Yes. I’ve been told,’ Helena muttered. ‘But even good people are capable of dark deeds.’ Her mother’s face flickered like a distant dream. She blinked and dispelled the haunting memories to focus on her present troubles. ‘Regardless of whether she is guilty of murder or not, she is certainly at fault for blocking my powers. If I could hear her thoughts, maybe I could clear her of this crime. Is it so hard to believe I might be trying to help her?’

events.did: 姨妈反问「是吗」；海伦娜说「我是在试图弄清真相，这怎么会把我画成反派」；姨妈指出「因为你早就认定伯罗斯夫人就是反派」，并说她很擅长揭露令人不适的现实——只要不涉及她自己的生活
events.verbatim: Aunt Rowan narrowed her gaze over her own steaming cup of bergamot-infused black tea. ‘Are you?’ ‘I am trying to determine the truth. How does this paint me the villain?’ ‘Because you have already pre-determined that Lady Burrows is the villain.’ Aunt Rowan was annoyingly good at exposing uncomfortable realities. As long as they didn’t pertain to her own life.

events.did: 哈姆雷特温热的身体靠着她的小腿；她一口气认输：「行！我就是不喜欢她。她把 Clio 从我们身边抢走了。她正在变成埃莉最好的新朋友。连我那该死的魔宠都把脑袋搁在她那条花边裙的膝上。」
events.verbatim: Hamlet’s warm body leaned against Helena’s leg. ‘Fine! I don’t like her. Is that what you want me to say? She has taken Clio away from us. She is becoming Ellie’s new best friend. Even my bloody familiar is putting his head in her frilly lap.’

events.did: 埃莉张大了嘴，罗恩姨妈的视线变得锐利；桌下传来哈姆雷特的咔哒低吼
events.verbatim: Ellie’s mouth fell open as Aunt Rowan’s gaze sharpened. Hamlet’s clicking growl could be heard under the table.

events.did: 反问「哈姆雷特做了什么？」；叙述者点出姨妈终于开始理解海伦娜对伯罗斯夫人那完全正当的偏见
events.verbatim: ‘Hamlet did what?’ Finally, her aunt was beginning to understand Helena’s very justifiable prejudice against Lady Cynthia Burrows.

events.did: 说「看吧？现在她又阻断了我的力量。也许她没有杀她丈夫，但她藏了东西。」
events.verbatim: ‘See? And now she is blocking my power. Maybe she isn’t guilty of killing her husband, but she is hiding something.’

events.did: 抚着奥菲利娅说「如果哈姆雷特信任她，那她藏的东西不会太糟」；蓝眼发亮（她有新主意时就这样）：「也许是你自己在阻断自己的力量。你对她的厌恶让你听不见她的念头。有女巫给自己下过咒吗，罗恩姨妈？」在姨妈回答前追问「能想象一个给自己下咒的女巫吗？」咯咯笑着指向海伦娜：「你有没有想过问题出在你身上，Hel？」
events.verbatim: ‘If Hamlet trusts her, then whatever she is hiding can’t be all that bad.’ Ellie absently stroked Ophelia’s body. The ferret fairly hummed with satisfaction. Ellie’s blue eyes brightened, as they were wont to do when she had a new idea. ‘Maybe you are blocking your own powers. Your dislike of her is stopping you from being able to hear her thoughts. Has a witch ever hexed herself, Aunt Rowan?’ Before their aunt could answer, Ellie continued. ‘Can you imagine a self-hexing witch?’ She giggled before pointing a finger at Helena. ‘Have you considered you might be the problem, Hel?’

events.did: 反驳「胡扯！我讨厌的人多了，读他们的心思照样没问题，佩斯特勒维特夫人就是。我要是不想听某个人的心思而去给自己下咒，她会排在我名单最前。」佩斯特勒维特夫人是他们最难缠的顾客之一，也是位血比亚得里亚海更蓝的公爵夫人，所以得通融
events.verbatim: ‘Bollocks to that! There are plenty of people I don’t like, and I can read their minds just fine. Lady Pestlewit for one. If I was going to hex myself to not hear someone’s thoughts, she would be at the top of my list.’ Lady Pestlewit was one of their most difficult customers. She was also a duchess with blood bluer than the Adriatic Sea, so allowances had to be made.

events.did: 说「让我做点研究。我有个朋友在林利斯哥巫团，可能帮得上忙。我明天给她写信。」
events.verbatim: Aunt Rowan tapped her finger on her lip. ‘Let me do some research. I have a friend in the Linlithgow coven who might be able to help. I’ll send her a letter on the morrow.’

events.did: 海伦娜皱眉「那不是在苏格兰吗？回信要好久」；姨妈笑说「傻女巫。我不用邮递」——作为土系女巫她能影响植物与动物，找一只自愿的有翼生物送信是小把戏
events.verbatim: Helena’s brow creased. ‘Isn’t that in Scotland? It’ll take ages to get a reply.’ ‘Silly witch. I’m not using the post.’ Aunt Rowan’s lips tilted in a smug smile. As an earthwitch, she could influence both flora and fauna. Finding a willing winged creature to carry her missive would be a simple trick.

events.did: 海伦娜说「我明天要讯问伯罗斯夫人。我要是听不见她在想什么，怎么帮拉奇兰叔叔？」；姨妈回「你是个女人。用你的直觉。你不需要任何特殊魔法来做到这点。」她的笑并不令人安慰
events.verbatim: ‘I’m interviewing Lady Burrows tomorrow. How can I help Uncle Lachlan if I can’t hear anything she’s thinking?’ ‘You’re a woman. Use your intuition. You don’t need any special magic for that.’ Aunt Rowan’s smile was not comforting.

events.did: 说「你仍然能听见其他所有人的心思。专注于他们。也许你能从仆役那里发现什么有用的。」拍拍她的手；「至于嫉妒辛西娅——」被海伦娜打断「我才不嫉妒」后，埃莉当作没被打断继续：「记住，我交的任何新朋友都取代不了我对你的爱，Hel。没有理由被她威胁。」
events.verbatim: ‘And you can still hear the thoughts of everyone else,’ Ellie replied cheerfully. ‘Focus on them. Maybe you’ll discover something from the staff that might help.’ She patted Helena’s hand, her kindness impossible to shake off. ‘As for feeling jealous of Cynthia⁠—’ ‘I’m not jealous.’ Ellie continued as though she hadn’t been interrupted. ‘Just remember, no new friend I make will ever replace the love I have for you, Hel. There’s no reason to be threatened by her.’

events.did: 自省：辛西娅威胁的不只是她在巫团里的自信；出于她无法理解的理由，辛西娅搅动了她灵魂里平静的水面；海伦娜一点也不喜欢
events.verbatim: Cynthia was threatening more than just Helena’s confidence in her coven. For reasons she couldn’t begin to understand, she was churning the calm waters of her soul. Helena didn’t like it. Not one bit.

events.did: 不停地摩擦裙上不均匀的黑色染色条痕；仓促的染色没能完全盖住那件曾是她最爱的日装——白底蓝花、领口与袖口有蕾丝；守丧的寡妇不可能在丈夫死后第二天穿这样明快鲜艳的颜色；洗衣女工时间紧迫尽力而为；辛西娅注意到手指上留下灰色痕迹，只能想象身体其余部分是什么样子
events.verbatim: Cynthia couldn’t stop rubbing the uneven streaks of black staining her skirt. The hasty dye job didn’t completely hide the pattern of what had once been her favourite day dress. A white and blue floral affair with lace around the collar and sleeves. Still, needs must and a widow couldn’t possibly be seen in such bright and cheerful colours the day after her husband’s death. Her laundress had done the best she could with so little time, but Cynthia noticed the grey aftermath on her fingers. She could only imagine what the rest of her body looked like.

events.did: 「我正在变成一个影子。或者，我一直都是。」
events.verbatim: I’m turning into a shadow. Or perhaps, I’ve always been one.

events.did: 盘算要订一整柜黑衣：黑一年，之后灰与薰衣草色再一年；两年的社交隔离，去哀悼一个从未在乎过她分毫的丈夫；即便死了休伯特仍在控制她，社会乐于做他的执行者；王国内没有一个贵族不会乐于在她不履行尽职守寡责任时谴责她
events.verbatim: She would need to order a new wardrobe in black. Black for a full year only to be followed by grey and lavender for another year. Two years of social isolation to mourn a husband who had never cared a whit about Cynthia. It was an insufferable fact that even in death, Hubert controlled her. And society was happy to act as his enforcer. There wasn’t a peer in the realm who wouldn’t leap at the chance to condemn Cynthia if she dared shirk her responsibilities as a dutifully mourning widow.

events.did: 「她还能得到自由吗？」
events.verbatim: Would she never be free?

events.did: 「若我不能说服麦克杜格尔警司相信我清白，就不能。被直接割席与脖子套绞索没法比。」
events.verbatim: I won’t if I can’t convince Superintendent MacDougal of my innocence. Being cut direct hardly compares to my neck in a noose.

events.did: 口袋里的吊坠沉甸甸抵着大腿；束腰让她难以深呼吸；臀垫莫名发痒；渴望解开上衣扣子、让阳光照在皮肤上；后颈一缕卷发发痒，她克制乱动的冲动
events.verbatim: The locket in her pocket hung heavy against her thigh. Her corset made it difficult to take a deep breath, and her bustle seemed unaccountably itchy. She longed to unbutton the top of her bodice and feel the sunlight on her skin. A curl tickled the back of her neck as she resisted the urge to fidget.

events.did: 问「茶，麦克杜格尔警司？」——对方摇头；再问「布莱尔小姐？」
events.verbatim: ‘Tea, Superintendent MacDougal?’ The gentleman shook his head. ‘Miss Blair?’

events.did: 海伦娜穿丝质蓝色日装；颜色让辛西娅想起浪头将起未起时的浪；衬出她灰色眼睛与带露水的皮肤；简洁剪裁凸显她修长身形
events.verbatim: Helena wore a silk blue day dress. The colour reminded Cynthia of a wave just before it crested. It set off the woman’s grey eyes and dewy skin while the simple cut brought attention to her long, lean lines.

events.did: 「她的腿一定长得没尽头。」随即脸颊发热、觉得这个念头不得体：「我这是怎么了？我该专注于哀悼，而不是想象她穿着丝袜的腿长什么样。」
events.verbatim: Her legs must go on forever. Cynthia’s cheeks heated at the inappropriate thought. What is wrong with me? I should be focusing on grieving, not trying to imagine what her legs look like in silk stockings.

events.did: 感到不是损失的酸痛，而是某种新的东西在灵魂里搅动——明亮闪烁的气泡，把周围的世界都改变了
events.verbatim: But instead of feeling the ache of loss, something new stirred within her soul. A bright, sparkling fizz that transformed the world around her.

events.did: 前一晚「发现」之后无法入睡；穿着衬裙坐在她最喜欢的窗台位置，俯瞰后花园，可以忘掉自己身处伦敦腹地；她看着银月从蓝黑的天空升起；推开窗，夜风拂面，肺像久违地这样张开；空气里有风信子与玫瑰的味道；画眉的歌萦绕在房间里；解脱如浪潮涌过她；生命在四周搏动；大地的心跳带来野性的自由，其规模令她恐惧
events.verbatim: Cynthia had been unable to sleep after her discovery the night before. Instead, she sat in her shift at her favourite spot on the windowsill. Overlooking the back gardens, she could forget she was in the heart of London. Breathless, she watched the silver moon rise in a blue-black sky. Opening the window, Cynthia bathed in evening breezes, her lungs expanding for what seemed like the first time in forever. Hyacinths and roses flavoured the air. The haunting melody of a song thrush filled her room, and relief swept through her like a wave. Life pulsed around her. The beat of the earth brought with it wild freedom, frightening in its magnitude.

events.did: 她记得这种久远的感觉：曾懂得小溪的低语、感受夏日阳光的温暖拥抱、在秋风里与树共舞；遗忘而自由地在父母乡间庄园的田野里狂奔了七个蒙福的年头；父母把孩子们留给一位和善但相当疏忽的保姆带大；她在户外的时间多于室内，在父亲无尽产业的林地中找到庇护
events.verbatim: She remembered this long-ago feeling. Once, she had understood the whispered stories of the bubbling brook, felt the warm embrace of summer’s sun, and danced with the trees in autumn’s wind. Forgotten and free, she ran wild in the fields of her parents’ country estate for seven blessed years. Her parents had left their children to be raised by a kind but rather negligent nanny. Cynthia spent more time out of doors than inside, finding her sanctuary in the wooded grounds of her father’s endless property.

events.did: 她曾经快乐，直到她生日那天一切改变：保姆被解雇、托马斯被送去上学、斯迈斯女教师到来
events.verbatim: She had been happy. Until her birthday when everything changed. Her nanny was dismissed, Thomas was sent away to school, and Governess Smithers arrived.

events.did: 淑女般的笑容与柔软的手掩住暴君的灵魂；她很快学会：合格的年轻淑女不把时间花在假装和田鼠说话或与蜜蜂分享秘密上；她迅速掌握了完美礼仪、家务技艺与无条件服从；白桦条教了她很多；十六岁离开乡间庄园去上 finishing school 时，她几乎记不得雨天午后坐在柳树下听大地呼吸是什么感觉
events.verbatim: A pleasant smile and soft hands hid the soul of a tyrant. Cynthia learned quickly that a proper young lady did not spend her time pretending to talk to field mice or sharing secrets with the bumblebees. She quickly mastered perfect manners, domestic accomplishments, and unwavering obedience. The birch switch taught her well, and when she left the country estate at sixteen for finishing school, she hardly remembered what it felt like to sit under the willow on a rainy afternoon and listen to the earth breathe.

events.did: 在守寡的第一夜，浸在银色月光里、夏夜歌声抚慰灵魂、完美有序的生活彻底碎裂，她开始记起来
events.verbatim: But on the first night of her widowhood, soaking up the silver moonlight, summer’s midnight song serenading her soul as her perfectly ordered life fantastically fractured, she started to remember.

events.did: 她不再受父亲、哥哥或丈夫的意志支配；被解开缰绳，能乘风飞往风吹去的任何地方
events.verbatim: No longer was she beholden to the will of her father, her brother, or her husband. She was untethered, able to fly on the wind wherever it might blow.

events.did: 「完全自由。」
events.verbatim: Completely free.

events.did: 「经历如此纯粹的狂喜之后，她怎么能装出悲伤？」
events.verbatim: How could she pretend sadness after experiencing such a rush of unadulterated joy?

events.did: 盘算未来或许不确定，但终于完全属于她自己，是一份荣耀的礼物；她得搬离现在的住所；会得到 Cotswold 附近的一座寡居宅邸、一条街外的小联排住宅，以及一笔远不及休伯特全部财富但足以让她余生过得很好的年金；还有她婚后保留的、来自父亲的遗产；休伯特的死给了她比做他妻子时更多独立与收入
events.verbatim: Her future might be uncertain, but it finally belonged solely to her. What a glorious gift. She would need to leave her current residence, but she would receive a dowager house near Cotswold, a tidy little townhouse a few streets away, and an annual income hardly comparable to Hubert’s total wealth, but certainly ample enough to ensure Cynthia would live very well for the remainder of her days. There were also funds she inherited from her father that Cynthia retained after her marriage. Hubert’s death had granted her more independence and income than she would have ever enjoyed as his wife.

events.did: 「除非我因谋杀他被定罪。」
events.verbatim: Unless I’m convicted of his murder.

events.did: 拒绝考虑这种可能；必须说服麦克杜格尔警司和他那让人恼火（漂亮）的侄女相信她清白；她手里握着脆弱而可惧的自由礼物，不会让给任何人
events.verbatim: She refused to consider the possibility. It was imperative she convince Superintendent MacDougal and his infuriating (beautiful) niece that she was innocent. Because she held the fragile and fearsome gift of freedom in her hands, and she wasn’t about to relinquish it to anyone.

events.did: 「当然不是那个能像海妖一样困住我的水系女巫。」
events.verbatim: Certainly not a waterwitch who could entrap me like a siren.

events.did: 被拉回当下：海伦娜伸手取杯碟，两人手指相触；萤火虫在辛西娅血液里爆发、穿过身体留下光的轨迹；翅膀的振动吻上她的胸口、拂过脉搏点、tickle 在乳房之下；这是最非凡的感受
events.verbatim: She was brought back to the present as Helena reached for the cup and saucer. Their fingers brushed together. Fireflies erupted in Cynthia’s bloodstream, racing through her body and leaving trails of light behind. The vibrations of their wings kissed her chest, flicked against her pulse points, and tickled just beneath her breasts. It was the most extraordinary thing.

events.did: 那股奇怪的能量沿着辛西娅窜流，比昨天更强，也诱人三倍
events.verbatim: The curious bolt of energy zinging through Cynthia was even more powerful than it had been yesterday, and thrice as enticing.

events.did: 「为什么海伦娜·布莱尔让我觉得自己像在触碰一道电流？」
events.verbatim: Why does Helena Blair make me feel like I’m touching a current of electricity?

events.did: 心跳加速，海伦娜的目光将她牢牢俘获；自问「她也感觉到了吗？」；随即否认「不可能。我是紧张，仅此而已。」
events.verbatim: Cynthia’s heart thumped loudly as Helena held her gaze captive. Did she feel it too? Impossible. I’m nervous. That’s all.

events.did: 灰眼闪光（让辛西娅想起昨夜月色，随后暗成更自然的颜色），靠回座位说「我们有几个问题要问你，伯罗斯夫人」；她的头发在盛夏里却有着秋天所有色彩的荣光，被阳光捕获；她本可以是卡吕普索，把辛西娅困在海沫失落的小岛上；但辛西娅不会屈服
events.verbatim: Helena’s grey eyes glimmered, reminding Cynthia of last night’s moon before darkening to a more natural colour. She sat back in her seat. ‘We have some questions for you, Lady Burrows.’ Her hair, all the glorious colours of autumn in the middle of summer, caught the sunlight. She could have been Calypso, holding Cynthia captive on an island lost in sea foam. But Cynthia would not succumb.

events.did: 决定先发制人：「我理解麦克拉奇兰警司为什么有话问我。我弄不明白的是你在这件事里的角色。」盯着海伦娜，忍住手不抖，喝了口茶：「告诉我，你施什么魔法？」语气刻意轻松，实则急切想知道
events.verbatim: Forcing her thoughts away from fancy, she determined to attack first. ‘I understand why Superintendent MacLachlan has questions for me. What I can’t puzzle out is your role in all of this.’ Cynthia held Helena’s gaze, refusing to let her hand tremble as she sipped her tea. ‘Tell me, what magic do you conjure?’ She kept her tone carefree, but she was desperate to know.

events.did: 哥哥曾告诉她，熟练的士兵总会先摸清敌人的长处以克服之；这建议很中肯；她昨晚差点问 Clio 海伦娜的能力，但那位聪明的女巫会对辛西娅的兴趣做过多解读，而她当时纯粹只想在这场调查中自保
events.verbatim: Her brother once told her that a skilled soldier always learned his enemy’s strengths so he could overcome them. It was sound advice. She had almost asked Clio the night before of Helena’s powers, but the clever witch would read too much into Cynthia’s interests when she was purely focused on protecting herself in this investigation.

events.did: 海伦娜握拳、眼中闪过危险的光；她想「会读心，多半没错。在挑逗一个女巫之前我该小心点」
events.verbatim: Helena fisted her hand and something dangerous flared in her eyes. Magic, no doubt. I suppose I should be careful before baiting a witch.

events.did: 但她不想再小心了；她想鲁莽而狂野；想找回那个久已失落的、困于规则与期待的孩子并抱紧；想站在风暴中心让风鞭打皮肤、让雨浸透灵魂
events.verbatim: Only, she didn’t want to be careful any more. She wanted to be reckless and wild. She wanted to find that child, lost so long ago to rules and expectations, and hold her close. She wanted to stand in the centre of the storm and let the wind whip her skin as the rain soaked her soul.

events.did: 「绞刑架的威胁最能让人看清轻重。」
events.verbatim: There’s nothing like the threat of a hangman’s noose to bring things into perspective.

events.did: 问「你不担心我的力量会吓到你？」；答「恐惧控制不了我」——至少她不想再让它控制自己；生命太短，不能困在惊惶里
events.verbatim: ‘Are you not worried my powers might frighten you?’ ‘Fear does not control me.’ At least, she didn’t want it to control her any longer. Life was too fleeting to waste trapped in trepidation.

events.did: 宣告「我读心思，伯罗斯夫人。」——本章末句
events.verbatim: ‘I read thoughts, Lady Burrows.’
